cosy-lesson.title: We’re Losing 338 Spoken Words Every Day

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Linguistic Decay – the gradual loss of words or grammatical structures in a language over time.

p.em: Example: Some experts are concerned about linguistic decay caused by rapid texting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Interaction – reciprocal action or influence between two or more people.

p.em: Example: Face-to-face interaction is essential for maintaining social skills.

cosy-blockquote.p: Monosyllabic – consisting of one syllable (often used to describe short, unhelpful answers).

p.em: Example: He gave a monosyllabic reply when I asked how his day was.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive Load – the amount of information that working memory can hold at one time.

p.em: Example: Deep conversation requires a higher cognitive load than simple messaging.

cosy-blockquote.p: Eloquence – fluent or persuasive speaking or writing.

p.em: Example: His eloquence made him a very effective public speaker.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vocabulary Range – the total number of different words a person knows and uses.

p.em: Example: Reading diverse books is the best way to expand your vocabulary range.

cosy-blockquote.p: Isolation – the state of being separate from others.

p.em: Example: Physical isolation is highly linked to cognitive decline in older seniors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nuance – a subtle difference in meaning, expression, or sound.

p.em: Example: A rich vocabulary allows you to express every small nuance of emotion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Digital Distraction – losing focus on a task or conversation because of a digital device.

p.em: Example: Digital distraction is often cited as a cause for shorter real-life conversations.

cosy-blockquote.p: Interpersonal – relating to relationships or communication between people.

p.em: Example: The company is looking for candidates with strong interpersonal skills.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the research, what specific parameters indicate that a rapid linguistic decay is taking place in modern communities?
★ What is lost when indigenous languages are no longer spoken by younger generations?

What evidence in the study shows that face-to-face interaction is crucial to prevent the erosion of rare words?
★ Do you prefer texting your friends or calling them on the phone for a quick chat?

According to researchers, what are the cognitive risks of a purely monosyllabic verbal habit in teenagers?
★ What is your favorite emoji, and does it help you express feelings better than words?

Based on the clinical observations, how does texting minimize the overall cognitive load during social communication?
★ When was the last time you had a truly deep, uninterrupted conversation that lasted hours?

How does the study map the correlation between standard reading habits and verbal eloquence?
★ Do you find it harder to concentrate on a long spoken story than you used to?

What data metrics prove that our overall vocabulary range has contracted significantly over the last decade?
★ Are there some complex feelings that you find completely impossible to put into words?

According to the paper, how does physical isolation accelerate native language attrition?
★ Do you speak differently when you are typing a message versus speaking out loud?

What findings show that young speakers are losing their appreciation for conversational nuance?
★ How do you react when someone gives you a very short, monosyllabic answer to a question?

How do scientists isolate the effects of digital distraction from general sociolinguistic evolution during testing?
★ Do you think reading physical books is the best way to expand your vocabulary?

What parameters define successful interpersonal communication in the study's experimental setup?
★ If you could only speak 500 words per day, who would you choose to talk to?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to validate rapid linguistic decay metrics, spoken language will be replaced entirely by direct brain-to-brain digital signals within a century.
★ Would you support a weekly 'no-screen, only-talking' day in your local community?

As our understanding of digital interaction limits develops, future generations will communicate almost entirely through custom visual animations.
★ Do you think written messaging is slowly destroying the art of public speaking?

Imagine future research shows that monosyllabic verbal constraints degrade emotional intelligence; public schools will enforce daily public debating requirements.
★ Can an automated writing assistant capture your unique voice and personality?

If we map the exact cognitive load required for high-variety talking, AI filters will automatically enrich our written texts with complex synonyms.
★ Will future generations communicate almost entirely through short video clips and emojis?

As preventative therapies are validated, high-variety eloquence will be recognized as a key indicator of cognitive health and mental resilience.
★ Would you trust an AI to summarize your friends' long audio messages for you?

Imagine future research proves that our vocabulary range dictates our memory span; brain-chips will automatically inject rare synonyms during live conversations.
★ Do you think our brains are slowly losing the ability to think in complex sentences?

If we can monitor how physical isolation restricts speech diversity, neighborhood robots will be deployed to initiate mandatory small-talk with lonely seniors.
★ Would you feel comfortable living in a society where silence is valued more than talking?

As communication models evolve, the subtle nuance of face-to-face talking will be fully coded into digital holograms.
★ Should schools ban text messaging on campus to force students to talk face-to-face?

Imagine future research shows that digital distraction permanent damages focus centers; wireless signals will be blocked inside all public libraries.
★ What is the most beautiful spoken word in your native language, and why?

As cryptographic protocols are simplified, traditional interpersonal relationships will require biometric verification nodes to establish authenticity.
★ Do you think the English language is becoming richer or poorer in the internet age?

ul.li: Incorrect: There is less words today → Correct: There are fewer words today ((Fewer for countable nouns))
Incorrect: It is a very good news → Correct: It is very good news ((Uncountable news))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
Incorrect: I have 25 years old → Correct: I am 25 years old ((Age with 'to be'))
